Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-09
Start: 14:30 UTC
End: 15:32 UTC (62m)
Location: Zoom
Record: Fireflies auto-transcript
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Apex Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Apex SRE), Rita Singh (Apex Product), Tim (Apex infra)

Summary: Quick follow-up after the 2026-03-06 production latency cascade. Goal was to align on mitigations (fallback routing, canary cadence, runbook updates), validate the proposed KV-cache hardening, and agree next steps for a short POC to reduce long-tail tail latency.

Topics: incident recap, root cause hypotheses (KV eviction + autoscaler loop), fallback routing (model variant fallthrough), canary rollout cadence, runbook & playbook updates, telemetry/alerts tuning, verification steps for staging POC.

[00:00] Sofia: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, trying to keep this tight we've got about an hour. quick recap — we put the postmortem notes in the doc, link in chat, and Daniel will walk the mitigation plan.
[00:28] Daniel: hi all, yeah hi, so first quick refresher, the outage on Friday was a 3.5 hour degradation where tails spiked for ~20% of tokens, this was correlated with a cascade in prefix cache eviction plus an aggressive horizontal autoscaler that kept spinning up cold workers. as a result requests hit cold kv misses and we saw 400-700ms extra p99.
[00:54] Maya: can i interrupt, i think the timeline had an overlap with our deploy window, we did push a small feature but the signals show the pattern started before the deploy.
[01:12] Daniel: yeah, agree, deploy likely contributed to traffic profile but not the root cause, we believe the primary vector was an interplay between our prefix cache TTL and an autoscaler policy that mistakenly used GPU memory free as a scale-down trigger. there was also a degraded kernel selection path on certain seq-len combos, a rare perf hole.
[01:42] Liam: logs show a ton of evict events right before the spike. we also got a flurry of internal retries from the customer client which amplified load.
[02:05] Sofia: noted — so today's mitigation plan has three pillars: immediate fallback routing (route to lower-capacity but warmed model shard), KV-cache hardening (increase TTL + protect hot keys), and autoscaler tweak (min replica floor + change metric to request_queue_length).
[02:40] Rita: the fallback routing — will that change inference quality? product is sensitive to hallucination changes, we need an SLO guardrail.
[02:56] Daniel: good question, the plan is to route only for latency-sensitive endpoints and to a variant of the same model quantized but validated for parity. we will also enable token-budgeted fallback so output truncation is controlled. quality delta measured in evals was small on our smoke tests but we'll run your prompt set.
[03:24] Tim: is this something we need to opt into? how will it affect billing?
[03:36] Sofia: no opt-in required for emergency fallback; in steady-state we can make it a config toggle per route, billing will be per-token for the variant model, we'll note any difference in the pricing sheet. we'll send a breakdown.
[03:54] [04:10] Daniel: workaround step 1: raise cache TTL for prefix v1 from 30s to 300s for the routes that saw the spike. workaround step 2: pin min_replicas=3 for that pool during business hours. long-term: we want to implement a warm-standby pool and a fast-restore flow that rehydrates KV from persistent cold-store faster.
[04:40] Maya: are there risks to extending TTL? could that increase stale outputs?
[04:50] Daniel: TTL is for KV prefix keys, it only affects internal prefix/kvcache not user-visible content, risk small but we will monitor.
[05:08] Liam: one thing we found odd — a sequence of 11-17 tokens caused the kernel to choose a slower attention path under one of the compiled kernels. we flagged that to Redwood ops.
[05:30] Daniel: yup that's the compilation corner-case i mentioned; our kernel selection table will be updated to prefer the optimized path for that seq-len or fall back to the faster algorithm. should be a microsecond fix but avoids the p99 step.
[05:52] Sofia: ok let's move into runbook changes, Daniel?
[06:00] Daniel: runbook changes: 1) new alert "kv_eviction_spike" threshold at >200 evictions/min for 3 mins -> trigger page. 2) automated mitigation job to bump TTL and pin replicas for 15 minutes while on-call investigates. 3) a manual rollback play for recent deploys with a fast switch to previous model version. we'll add a checklist for degraded kernel detection.
[06:42] Maya: for the automation, who can approve the job? our oncall will need ability to opt-out if it causes downstream effects.
[06:52] Daniel: we'll add an approval flag and dry-run mode. the automation will create a ticket in your jira and require a single confirm click.
[07:10] [07:38] Rita: on validation — can Redwood run our top-150 prompts through the fallback model and give a diff report? we want to evaluate any semantic regressions.
[07:52] Daniel: yes we can, please share the prompt corpus (or we'll pull from your eval bucket), we'll produce token-level diffs and a summary with examples.
[08:05] Liam: also, we want to test the repro locally, i've got a staging setup but need the exact repro steps for the kv corruption and the script that simulates the autoscaler behavior.
[08:24] Daniel: i'll attach the repro script to the postmortem doc; it's in the shared drive link. caution though transcription of the script had a small var name mismatch in the doc, we'll correct that.
[08:40] Sofia: quick note about telemetry: add a histogram for request service time by sequence-length bucket, that'll make these regressions visible earlier.
[08:58] Maya: agreed. we'll also lower the paging threshold so we get a page at p99>250ms not p99>400ms.
[09:14] [09:35] Tim: curious — are there any known issues with dedup caching and our CDN? could cold client side caches produce spikes that look like server cold starts?
[09:50] Daniel: yes that's possible; we're going to add a synthetic that warms both application and server caches in staging. also we recommend reducing TTL on CDN for a few minutes during deploy windows so we don't get simultaneous cache misses.
[10:12] Liam: what's the expected impact on cost if we pin min replicas and keep TTL higher? need an estimate.
[10:23] Sofia: rough estimate for the pool is +6-9% cost during business hours; we'll send a detailed delta in the cost calc spreadsheet.
[10:36] [11:00] Daniel: question about audit & compliance — any requirement to log all fallback events for your auditors? we can add an event stream for that.
[11:12] Maya: yes please, we need a tamper-evident log of fallback invocations and who triggered the automation. include request ids and model variant ids.
[11:26] Daniel: we'll emit an append-only event to your SIEM endpoint and include S3 archival with MD5 checksums.
[11:38] Rita: i want to make sure we run a scheduled P0 test that simulates the long-tail every Friday on staging so product can see the behaviour.
[11:52] Daniel: happy to set that up. we'll create a k8s job that runs the synthetic spine test and produces a report.
[12:05] Sofia: ok can we recap actions and owners?
[12:12] Daniel: yes: Daniel to draft fallback playbook and attach to postmortem doc (due 3/12); Redwood to run apex prompt set through fallback and return diffs (due 3/14); Apex to run staging synthetic and send logs (due 3/16); Redwood to update autoscaler policy and provide config diff (due 3/12).
[12:46] Maya: i'll also open a ticket to adjust paging threshold and confirm our oncall acknowledgement process.
[13:00] [13:30] Sofia: any blockers on Redwood side?
[13:36] Daniel: only the kernel soft-fix; it's low-risk and we can ship it as a patch this week. we may need a brief maintenance window for the pool switch — will coordinate.
[13:52] Tim: can we get a war-room slack channel? makes coordination easier.
[13:59] Sofia: creating #apex-redwood-warroom now and will invite folks.
[14:08] Maya: thanks everyone, this was useful. expect the postmortem + runbook link in your inbox.
[14:20] Sofia: i'll also ping pricing and send the cost delta spreadsheet.
[14:30] Daniel: wrapping — one last item, we'll enable more granular token-level logging for 48 hours during the next staging run to gather data.
[14:44] Sofia: perfect. thanks all.
